classification.difficultyReason: Express three related ages using the supplied n, interpret the sum being 11 less than the father's age, and solve before recovering all ages.

content.prompt: Let $n$ be the age of a student (in years). The student’s sister is 3 years older than the student, and the student’s father is 25 years older than the student. The sum of the ages of the student and his sister is 11 less than the age of their father. Find the ages of the student, his sister and their father.

answer.short: Student: 11 years; sister: 14 years; father: 36 years.
answer.worked:
The sister’s age is $n+3$ years and the father’s age is $n+25$ years.
$$\begin{align*}n+(n+3)&=(n+25)-11\\2n+3&=n+14\\2n+3-n&=n+14-n\\n+3&=14\\n&=11\end{align*}$$
The student is 11 years old, his sister is $11+3=14$ years old and their father is $11+25=36$ years old.

Check: $11+14=25$ and $36-11=25$, so the sum of the student’s and sister’s ages is 11 less than their father’s age.
